teaser.en: Brush against its pods and you will be scratching for hours: the hairs on this bean cause intense itching.

summary.en: *Uphupu* is the velvet bean, a vigorous climber with dark purple flowers and pods coated in stinging hairs. Its pods are best admired from a distance.

about.en:
*Uphupu* is a vigorous climbing bean that can smother shrubs and small trees. Its leaves have three broad leaflets, like most beans.

The flowers are dark purple and hang in long sprays. They are followed by curved pods covered in dense golden-brown or orange hairs. These hairs break off easily and cause intense itching on skin.

where.en: Look for *uphupu* in bush and on forest edges, climbing over other plants. The hairy pods are easiest to see as they ripen after the rains.

uses.en: No specific Digo use has been recorded. Elsewhere, cultivated forms of the velvet bean are grown as cover crops and the seeds, after careful processing, are eaten.

names.en: Digo: *uphupu*. English: velvet bean, buffalo bean or cowitch. No Swahili name has been recorded. Scientists call it *Mucuna pruriens*; *pruriens* means 'itching'.

reason.en: Lablab bean, a climbing bean grown for food
Climbing legume of the same bush
